summary: S34 asked for a verify gate papers already had. The gate existed (S32, ca23738a) and the survey already counted papers as gated; S33 had already retired the tests_only allowance the item asked to remove. The premise was stale on arrival. Delivered instead: the two defects that closing the hole created, plus two found while fixing them.

findings.claim: the filed debt was already closed; do not write a second gate
findings.evidence: gates.survey(): papers in gated[], kind=verify, name=verify.py. monitor/tests/test_gates.py:159 pins tests_only == {'verify-lab'}; papers is absent. Contrary to the item's prediction, test_gates.py does not go red once -- the sets it pins are unchanged by this work.

findings.claim: papers/verify.py reds on any committed top-level directory under papers/, including the runs/ CLAUDE.md mandates
findings.evidence: old paper_dirs() returned every subdirectory not starting with . or __. Reproduced at 71e9dc00: mkdir papers/runs/probe -> 'FAIL runs ships no gate', exit 1. at base commit c54954d6, `git ls-tree -r --name-only c54954d6 | grep -cE '(^|/)runs/'` is 3870 across 22 top-level directories (the first draft said 3706 and bound it to no command; that figure reproduces at no commit on this branch's ancestry -- corrected in the cycle-35 pass, see D5).
findings.adversarial_correction: Latent, never fired. grep 'red in papers' monitor/ci/merge.log is empty: this territory's provenance has always gone to papers/phase1-workshop/runs/, one level below where paper_dirs() looked. On the branch path it would fail the offending branch, not master. Not runs/-specific.

findings.claim: adding verify.py retired papers' own test suite from merge gating
findings.evidence: gates.py:192 gate_for() returns in the find_gate branch and never reaches has_tests() at :213. merge.log:1856 (15:02:51Z) ran pytest:papers once; :1872 (15:55:51Z) switched to verify:papers(verify.py); :1894/:1938/:1948 all verify. So pytest:papers ran once ever over test_uncited_gate.py's 62 tests; test_bare_gate.py's 20 arrived at 18:02:35Z and have never been run by CI.
findings.adversarial_correction: Not a displacement anyone could see: S32 authored verify.py at 11:03Z when papers held no test at all, and P16's suite arrived at 15:02Z in between. The loss lives only in the merge order. The precedent was already in writing -- test_gates.py:163-166 records the identical event for proxy and says the only reason it was acceptable is that proxy/verify.py:260 re-invokes the superseded gate.

findings.claim: gates.py's negative-sample declaration can be shadowed by a gate's own prose
findings.evidence: NEGATIVE_SAMPLE.search (gates.py:160) takes the first match anywhere in the file. This gate's docstring discusses the mechanism, so survey() read the declared sample as a single backtick: {'declared': '`', 'exists': False}. Failed safe here; would not have if the prose had named an existing path. Filed as monitor/inbox/20260729T231500Z-RES-2-negative-sample-shadowed-by-prose.md -- gates.py is monitor's.

findings.claim: the delegator had three more silences, all found by an adversarial audit and fixed here
findings.evidence: --timeout was parsed and passed to nothing, and even once applied its 1800 default matched ci_merge.py:543's own 1800 kill, so the outer kill always won (now 1500); sub-gates got no PYTHONPATH, the entitlement gates.gate_env() states, so it held under ci_merge and not under the documented human invocation; a gate exiting 0 with no output printed '(no output)' on the ok line and took the territory green. The recursion guard could also have skipped stage 3 while still exiting 0, so it now refuses to fire outside pytest.

findings.claim: this delivery's own gate printed a green line asserting a check that had not executed -- the defect class D2/D4/stage 3 exist to catch, committed by the gate about itself
findings.evidence: Probe A, cycle 35. THEORIA_PAPERS_VERIFY_INNER=1 alone is refused (RED, exit 1). INNER=1 plus PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST=<any> skips stage 3, exits 0, and printed "papers: green -- 1 paper(s), each gated by its own check, and the checks' own suite run". The skip itself is unavoidable (same shape as the legitimate nested run; the alternative to exiting 0 is a fork bomb) and two variables no merge sets is a narrow door. The false sentence was not. Undetected through cycles 33 and 34 because every test asserted on run_suite()'s return value or the exit code and nothing read the sentence.
findings.fix: run_suite() returns (ok, detail, ran). `ran` must be a third value because `ok` cannot carry it -- the skip is genuinely green -- and is returned rather than sniffed out of detail's prose so the caller cannot get it wrong. main() prints "...suite NOT run (stage 3 skipped)" on that path. Five suite call sites updated to the 3-tuple, each now also asserting `ran`, which was the missing assertion. Pinned by test_the_skipped_summary_does_not_claim_the_suite_ran; restoring the unconditional "run" reds that test and only that one (1 failed, 25 passed).

stage_3_is_not_decorative.method: mutate phase1-workshop/verify_paper.py MIN_ANCHOR 24 -> 0 (one of three guards the audit showed could be deleted with papers still green), run cd papers && python verify.py, restore
stage_3_is_not_decorative.result: stage 2 green (verify_paper: PASS 6/6), stage 3 red (pytest exited 1: 1 failed, 73 passed), gate exit 1. Before this change the same mutation merged. verify_paper.py restored byte-for-byte, git diff clean.

delegator_suite_is_not_decorative.claim: the delegator's own suite is load-bearing, not decoration
delegator_suite_is_not_decorative.method: four independent mutations of papers/verify.py, each reverted after; run papers/test_verify_delegator.py
delegator_suite_is_not_decorative.result: 4/4 caught, each by the test named for that property rather than by a blanket failure: 'if not tail:'->'if False:' reds test_a_gate_that_says_nothing_is_red (1 failed, 24 passed); MIN_PAPERS 1->0 reds test_no_paper_at_all_is_red_not_a_vacuous_pass + test_provenance_alone_does_not_satisfy_the_floor (2 failed, 23 passed); NO_TESTS_COLLECTED 5->999 reds test_a_vanished_suite_is_red (1 failed, 24 passed); strays.append->skipped.append reds test_an_unrecognised_directory_is_still_red + test_a_directory_without_the_marker_is_not_silently_dropped (2 failed, 23 passed). git diff verify.py clean after.

citation_audit.claim: every citation in RUN_STATE.md and the docstring resolves
citation_audit.method: Probe B, cycle 35: read each cited line; re-derive each count by collection or by git ls-tree
citation_audit.result: Resolve as claimed: gates.py :160/:177/:192/:213, test_gates.py :159/:163-166, ci_merge.py:543 (the 1800s kill), proxy/verify.py:260, and merge.log :1838/:1856/:1872/:1875/:1894/:1938/:1948. grep -c 'red in papers' merge.log still 0. All five quoted test names exist. Counts by collection: test_uncited_gate.py 62, test_bare_gate.py 20, test_verify_delegator.py 26. TWO WRONG, both corrected: (1) 3706 files under */runs/ reproduces at no commit on this ancestry -- 3870 at c54954d6 by (^|/)runs/, 3745 by ^[^/]+/runs/; the claim it supports holds at all three figures, which is why it survived two readings; docstring and RUN_STATE now carry the query and the commit. (2) RUN_STATE said '23 tests' in one sentence and '25 passed' in another; now 26 in both.
